To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the gamut volume and gamut surface are better approximated by computing the "local" convex-hull in CIELAB, rather than the "global" hull, and (2) the gamut surface can be computed via ray-tracing, and the gamut volume can be computed by integrating the gamut surface over the hue angle.

The proposed method for gamut characterization is based on the computation of the local convex hull in the device space, followed by the ray tracing in CIELAB to determine the maximum achievable chromas for a set of L and hue pairs.
